objective: Re-issued at base commit 70c1329, after the owner committed the temporary restricted worker source-write grant; the earlier proposal was written at an older commit and can no longer be approved. Speed and Reliability Foundation, corrected proposal that supersedes plan 1.2, which could not run because its validator names were prose and the governed worker had no write authority over ProjectOS source. Goal: make routine governed ProjectOS changes complete in seconds or minutes instead of tens of minutes, without weakening full validation or any existing owner gate. Exactly four phases in this order: validation-cache, doctor-preflight, gatekeeper-replay, readiness-evidence. The owner has already taken these decisions; carry them as fixed constraints and do not ask them again: (1) prerequisite, taken by the owner outside this plan before phase one runs: the governed worker's write grant is widened to ProjectOS source under projectos and its tests and docs, and never to .projectops authority, plan, decision, ledger or credential records, never to secrets; (2) performance targets on the reference machine, this development PC running Windows 11, Node 24.14.1 and Rust 1.96 against this repository, environment details recorded with the benchmark: warm unchanged validation 2 seconds or less, proof or data-only validation 5 seconds or less, targeted ProjectOS source validation 60 seconds or less where safely possible, Doctor 10 seconds or less, gatekeeper replay 2 seconds or less with zero provider spend; full uncached validation remains authoritative and is never weakened to hit a timing target; (3) cache version one is local and repository-scoped only, no shared developer or CI cache, at most 1 GB per governed repository, entries unused for 7 days expire, LRU cleanup when over budget, disposable and rebuildable, containing no secrets, credentials, raw provider prompts or responses, with content and integrity hashes required, and a corrupt or unreadable cache is a miss that runs; deleting the cache may reduce performance and must never reduce correctness; (4) dependency safety is constitutional: known unchanged may use a cache hit, known changed runs, unknown runs, corrupt runs, version or environment mismatch runs, and probably-unrelated never skips; the cache key must cover validator source, helpers and transitive code, declared and observed inputs, relevant configuration, schema and runtime version and the platform contract, and unknown dependency coverage fails toward run; (5) Doctor is mandatory before autonomous governed execution, paid gatekeeper dispatch and automatic technical commit or push continuation, and advisory-only for Control Center browsing, read-only inspection and local preview; (6) gatekeeper replay fixtures are redacted, normalised derivations of real accepted gatekeeper interactions, especially the four committed B9 decision records, committing only the minimum contract data needed, plus synthetic adversarial cases, with no credentials, raw provider prompts, unnecessary full provider responses or secret-shaped material; (7) readiness-evidence is benchmark plus evidence plus a READY or NOT READY verdict for the Forge autonomy proof and nothing more, not another hardening programme, and Forge Programme C does not start automatically: the owner takes one separate programme-transition decision afterwards. Validators are mechanically binding in this project, so set expectedValidators to exactly the single name validate-no-secrets for validation-cache, doctor-preflight and gatekeeper-replay, and to exactly the single name validate-all for readiness-evidence; the project's configured test suites run in every phase regardless. Protected actions remain owner-gated throughout: no production deployment, database mutation, messaging, payment, credential creation or disclosure, force push or merge.
